text:
### Observed differences

- Before, exactly one of three activities — A19 (about 33 in 100 cases), A20 (about 29 in 100) and A25 (about 40 in 100) — was executed in virtually every case, and the three almost never occurred together; in the later window each appears in only about 1 of 200 cases. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL001, REL002, REL006]
- Before, this block sat either directly after A27 (A27 led to A25/A19/A20 in about 44 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) or directly after A28 (A28 led to one of them in about 53 in 100), and the block always ran before A29; in the later window A27 leads to A28 in about 98 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and A28 leads to A29 in about 97 in 100. [DIR005, DIR006, REL003, REL005, REL012]
- Before, A19, A20 and A25 each routed mainly to A29 and A28 (for example A20 went to A29 in about 61 in 100 and A28 in about 38 in 100 of its outgoing transitions); in the later window these routing profiles vanish, with each activity's single residual occurrence leading elsewhere (A38, A37, A31) and the A28-to-A25 gap jumping from 1 to 5 positions — each based on one observation. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG003]
- Positions along the remaining chain tightened: A27 reached A29 typically 3 steps later before (about 90 in 100 cases) but typically 2 steps later afterwards (about 96 in 100); the A27-to-A28 and A28-to-A29 gaps collapsed to 1 step in about 96–98 in 100 cases, from roughly half that before. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG004]
- Separately, A10's outgoing transitions redistributed: before they concentrated on A15 (about 20 in 100), A47 and A16 (about 17 each) and A45 (about 14); afterwards the profile is more dispersed, led by A26 (about 17) and A45 (about 15) with many new, individually small targets, based on 35 versus 53 observed outgoing transitions. [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the three-way alternative block of A19, A20 and A25 — which before ran exactly once per case, inserted either between A27 and A28 or between A28 and A29 — is no longer executed, so that A27 now leads directly to A28 and A28 directly to A29, shortening that segment by one step. The participation of all three activities collapsed from about 29–40 in 100 cases to about 1 in 200, their incoming and outgoing edges disappeared in favour of the direct A27→A28 and A28→A29 edges, every pairwise relation with A27/A28/A29 switched from near-always co-occurrence to those activities running alone, and the positional distances shortened exactly as a one-activity removal predicts. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, LAG001, LAG002, LAG004]

With 25 qualifying control-flow items against roughly 0.5 expected without change, chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole, and the items are direct (participation, successor and relation changes) rather than indirect. [screening]

Limitation: the later window shows the block was not observed, not that it was removed from the process — it may still exist but never be triggered; the residual occurrences with new successors rest on a single trace each. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG003]

Other differences: A10's outgoing transition mix became noticeably more dispersed in the later window; this redistribution is not part of the main hypothesis, and with only 35 versus 53 observed transitions a sampling difference is a competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out. [DIR001]
